_note: ⛔ SNG-403. LOCAL LAYOUTS. Erik: 'the docks in millbrook on the river, the smithy, the fields.' ⚠️ THE TERRAIN GENERATOR HAS NOTHING AT THIS SCALE — its finest feature is ~0.3° ≈ 33 km and a village spans ~0.01° ≈ 1 km. So a local map is NOT a further zoom of the world raster; it is a NEW layer. ⛔ BUT IT IS NOT INVENTED EITHER: the world layer supplies the DIRECTIONS, and everything here is placed against them. That is the pattern the detailing engine should learn.
_frame: `localMap: {bearing, metres}` from the settlement centre. Bearing 0 = toward the pole (up-map), 90 = east. ⚠️ METRES, not degrees — a village is 400-800 m across and degrees at that scale are unreadable. The engine converts: dLat = metres·cos(bearing)/111320, dLon = metres·sin(bearing)/(111320·cos(lat)).
_derivation: ⛔ THE THREE GRADIENTS THE WORLD ALREADY KNOWS, measured at each settlement: (1) RIVER BEARING and distance — from the traced hydrology; (2) UPHILL BEARING — sample the generator's raw elevation around the point; (3) ROAD BEARINGS — from connections' worldPos. ⚠️ Water trades go riverward. Terraces and orchards go uphill. Fields take the flat. Gates and markets sit on the road bearings. Everything else fills the middle.

millbrook._reading: Its own seed names them and nobody made them places: 'Water wheels turn along the Echo River; terraced gardens climb the lower slopes. THE VILLAGE WELL AND THE RIVER DOCK ARE THE TWO CENTRES of daily life.' ⛔ Two centres is a LAYOUT INSTRUCTION and it has been sitting in the prose.

sites.name: The Village Well
sites.why: ⛔ One of the two centres the seed names. It IS the centre — bearing and distance zero.

sites.name: The River Dock
sites.why: ⛔ The other centre. ON THE RIVER BEARING — the one placement the world layer dictates outright.

sites.name: The Water Wheels
sites.why: Downstream of the dock on the same water. ⚠️ Wheels go below the landing so the boats are not fighting the race.

sites.name: The Terraced Gardens
sites.why: ⛔ 'Climb the lower slopes' — placed on the MEASURED UPHILL BEARING, not a guess.

sites.name: The Irrigation Fields
sites.why: ⚠️ The flat: opposite the uphill, and off the river so the ditches can run TO them. The encounterFlavor is farmers arguing about irrigation shares — this is what they are arguing over.

sites.name: The Smithy
sites.why: On the road out to Echo River Crossing. ⚠️ A smith sits where the carts already stop, and near enough the water to quench.

sites.name: Mara Wells' Store
sites.why: ⛔ ALREADY A PLACE, promoted from play, and sitting at Millbrook's EXACT coordinates — CCode's 'a room's position is a duplicate' finding, live. Now it stands between the well and the road, which is where a village store stands.

sites.name: The Commons
sites.why: Between the well and the dock — the ground people cross going from one centre to the other, which is what a commons IS.

echo_river_crossing._dataFlag: ⛔ ITS NEAREST TRACED RIVER IS 3.83° AWAY — about 425 km — AND ITS ENTIRE IDENTITY IS A BRIDGE OVER THE ECHO. `waterauth.json` authors a river here and the built hydrology does not carry one to it. ⚠️ I am placing the bridge on the fiction, not on the measurement, and flagging the gap rather than quietly bending the layout around bad data. SNG-403b.

sites.name: The Stone-and-Cable Bridge
sites.why: ⛔ The town IS the bridge. Centre by definition; everything else is which END you are on.

sites.name: The Old Bridge-Stone
sites.why: 'The old bridge-stone at the crossing is a waygate, and the least ceremonious one in the world — carters queue behind it.' ⚠️ A QUEUE IS A PLACEMENT: it sits at the bridge mouth, not off to one side.

sites.name: The Carters' Queue
sites.why: ⛔ On the Millbrook road bearing — the queue forms along the road people arrive by.

sites.name: The Empty Fisher Shacks
sites.why: ⚠️ 'Fisher shacks stand empty' — riverward and UPSTREAM, where the contamination is worst. They are empty for a reason and the position says why.

sites.name: The Granite Shoulders
sites.why: On the measured uphill — 'where the river narrows between granite shoulders'.

sites.name: The Survey Camp
sites.why: ⚠️ Contamination teams from Heights and Plateau, camped apart from the town and from each other.

greyhearth._reading: 'A town that buries for every road that meets here — the Crossing's dead and the Palelands' both.' ⛔ A BURYING TOWN'S LAYOUT IS ITS TRAFFIC: the dead arrive by road and go uphill.

sites.name: The Receiving Yard
sites.why: ⛔ On the Crossing road. The dead arrive from where the roads meet, so the yard faces that way.

sites.name: The Burying Grounds
sites.why: ⛔ UPHILL, on the measured bearing — drainage. Every real burying ground sits above its town.

sites.name: The Grey Hearth
sites.why: The town's name and its centre — the fire that gives the trades their work.

sites.name: The Singers' Hall
sites.why: 'Everyone here has sung over one.' ⚠️ Between the hearth and the grounds — on the walk.

sites.name: The Quiet Road
sites.why: ⛔ On the bearing to the Quiet Ground, which is where the dying go BEFORE. The two towns are one process.

the_cogitarium._verticalFinding: ⛔ THIS ONE BREAKS THE HORIZONTAL FRAME AND IT SHOULD. Its two promoted places are an ENTRANCE HALL and a THIRD TERRACE — the same footprint at different heights. ⚠️ AN INTERIOR NEEDS A VERTICAL AXIS. `localMap` needs an optional `level`: 0 ground, positive up, negative below. Without it the Cogitarium's two rooms land on top of each other and the map says they are the same place.

sites.name: Cogitarium Entrance Hall
sites.why: ⛔ On the Middle Way road bearing — an entrance faces the road people arrive by. Ground level.

sites.name: Cogitarium Third Terrace
sites.why: ⛔ LEVEL 3 — it is the THIRD terrace and the name says so. Uphill side, because a terrace climbs the slope it is cut into.

_generalisation: ⛔ FOUR LAYOUTS, FOUR DIFFERENT SHAPES, AND THE RULES ARE THE SAME THREE GRADIENTS. Millbrook: two centres named in its own prose, water trades riverward, terraces uphill, fields on the flat. Echo River Crossing: the bridge IS the centre and everything is which end you are on. Greyhearth: a burying town's plan is its traffic — dead arrive by road, go uphill. The Cogitarium: ⚠️ VERTICAL, and it broke the frame usefully. ⛔ NOTHING HERE WAS INVENTED FREELY: every placement cites either a measured bearing or a sentence already in the location's own seed. That is the constraint the engine must inherit — a generated layout that cannot cite a gradient or a line of prose is decoration.
